question: The sides of two squares are (4 + sqrt{3}) cm and (4 - sqrt{3}) cm, respectively. What is the sum of the areas of these two squares?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use identity: (a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²)

Here a = 4, b = √3

⇒ Sum of areas = 2(4² + (√3)²)

= 2(16 + 3) = 2 × 19 = 38

**∴ Answer = 38 cm²**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sides = (4 + √3) cm and (4 − √3) cm

**Formula used:**

Area of square = side²

**Calculation:**

⇒ Area₁ = (4 + √3)² = 16 + 3 + 8√3 = 19 + 8√3

⇒ Area₂ = (4 − √3)² = 16 + 3 − 8√3 = 19 − 8√3

⇒ Sum = (19 + 8√3) + (19 − 8√3)

⇒ = 38

**∴ The correct answer is 38 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Identity Used

(a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²)

Square Expansion

(a ± b)² = a² ± 2ab + b²

Simplification Trick

Opposite surds cancel when added

Application

Useful in symmetric algebraic expressions
